newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Former gov-general to head Century Zinc talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Former gov-general to head Century Zinc talks.

text.p: Queensland premier Rob Borbidge said on Friday that former Australian Governor-General Bill Hayden had accepted the position of facilitating negotiations with local Aboriginal groups over the RTZ-CRA A$1 billion Century zinc project in far north Queensland.
"Former governor-general Bill Hayden has accepted the role of facilitating negotiations under the Native Title Act re the Century project," Borbidge said in a statement.

The appointment follows earlier statements by the Borbidge government and RTZ-CRA subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd that negotiations were proceeding between Aboriginal communities, the companies and state government officials on land right problems that had stalled the huge Century Zinc project.
The state, which had been preparing enabling legislation to deliver security of land tenure to Century, withdrew its legislative programme in July at the request of RTZ-CRA.
Negotiations which commenced between Century Zinc and Aboriginal groups on August 5, are still proceeding under provisions of the Native Title Act.
The negotiations are expected to last four months with a six-month arbitration process allowed if agreement was not reached by December 5.
Century has warned that the longer the negotiating process takes the less the chance of supplying zinc from the project to the Netherlands' Budel smelter.
Pasminco Ltd was to be Century's biggest customer, purchasing half of the planned low-iron bearing zinc concentrates for the Budel smelter.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operations of Budel, whose current licence requires it to halt the production of jarosite, a zinc process residue, by June 1998.
Hayden told reporters he was pleasantly surprised by the appointment, describing his new task "an interesting challenge."
He said he would be visiting the area in the next few weeks.
"Letter will be going out to the various parties telling them of the need to come together for discussions," he said.
